newsitem.title: UK: Smiths gains after bullish analysts' visit.
newsitem.headline: Smiths gains after bullish analysts' visit.

text.p: Smiths Industries Plc shares put on 14p to 782-1/2p on Thursday after analysts took a positive view following an upbeat company visit on Wednesday, aerospace analysts said.
"Basically the inference was that the aerospace business will surprise on the upside in the next two years. The industry in general is going ballistic," said one analyst.
"And although we haven't changed our figures, people came away reassured about forecasts and strategy being on course," he said.
Several brokers reiterated positive trading views on the stock today.
Smiths new chief executive, Keith Butler-Wheelhouse, and other senior executives gave presentations to thirty analysts visiting Smiths' UK aerospace centre at Cheltenham.
"Butler-Wheelhouse looks like he'll give a more aggressive drive and they were positive on current trading," said the analyst.
Another analyst said that Smiths is benefitting from its higher proportion of U.S. business than others in the sector.
"Smiths benefits from having strong ties in U.S. aerospace, notably Boeing, which shields them from what's happening in Europe and that's been supporting the price recently," he said.
"For instance if the socialists get in in France that'll hold up the privatisation of their aerospace business but it'll hold Smiths back less than others," he said.

Private polls show the French Socialists are well-placed for victory in Sunday's election. The Socialists are expected to proceed more slowly in bringing in needed economic reforms to overhaul France's self-regulated, state-dominated economy.
